Resolves #21935

🌿 A dock projection that stalls can no longer stall without naming the flight it waits on.

`Reconciler.reconcileProjection` awaited its flights without a name: the staged shell's and the host's component updates, ancestor and bar commits, the held reveals, and the overflow recapture. Every later projection queues behind the current one (`waitedForTail`), so one flight that never settled froze the workspace, and its receipt named only the phase. In CI this was `WorkstationBoot.spec.mjs` failing 8 of 39 `components (3/3)` runs on 22 Nov (Mnemosyne's count on #21914), always with the predecessor stopped after `released`.

Each await now goes through `settleFlight`, which stamps the refresh's cycle `<name>Started` as the wait begins and `<name>` once the flight settles. `timing.awaiting` names the wait in flight until that wait ends, whether it settles or rejects (`Cycle#beginWait`). The Workspace passes its cycle (`Workspace.mjs`, one line), so a stall's receipt names the flight it waits on. This holds even inside an ancestor loop that waits under one name twice, where a held second wait would sit beside a first one that already stamped its pair (Sophie's replay, A2A f5d63857). No flight is left behind. The first two heads bounded the waits. Sophie's exact-owner replays (A2A cfa6d368, cab09fb4) showed that a held component update keeps its update latch (`VdomLifecycle.mjs:477–479,528`), and a held overflow read keeps the strip mid-measure (`Overflow.mjs:912–936`), whatever the waiter does. Ending a held flight under its owner, with Reset rendering behind it, is #21974, and these stamps name the flight it starts from.

size-guard-growth: src/dashboard/dock/Workspace.mjs — one key, `cycle`, in the projection options: the reconciler needs the refresh's cycle to stamp its flights; no logic moves into the file.

Evidence: L3 (unit arms; component tier on local Chromium, unthrottled and under 6× CPU throttle) → L3 required (AC-1 to AC-3). Residual: none for #21935; ending a held flight is #21974.

| AC-2 | CI-covered: the same spec's "settleFlight stamps a wait as it starts and as it settles, and names it in flight until it ends either way": a held flight is still waited on after 20 ms with `timing.awaiting` = `reconcileOverflow`, while a settled and a rejected wait leave no `awaiting`. "a held wait stays named after an earlier wait of the same name has stamped its pair" covers the ancestor loop. Red-proof: on `b3022249ce` no `awaiting` exists. |
| AC-3 | Outside CI, on this head's content: the two cold-boot Reset tests 20/20 with the cold page at 6× CPU throttle (`Emulation.setCPUThrottlingRate`, a local knob not in this diff), and the whole spec 40/40 unthrottled (`--repeat-each=5`). |

## Deltas from ticket

- AC-1 and AC-2 are proven at the unit tier rather than in a component spec: holding a flight inside a live Workstation needs a vdom-flight double the component tier does not have, and `settleFlight` is the one path every await takes.
- The stall did not reproduce locally (200 unthrottled runs at 6 and 16 workers, 20 Reset runs at 8× page throttle), so the first CI miss is the receipt: Post-Merge Validation.
